Which setting determines the baseline access a user has to records they do not own?
Organisation-wide defaults set the floor. Role hierarchy, sharing rules and manual sharing only ever open access up from there — they never restrict it.
How many fields per object can be tracked with standard field history tracking?
20 fields per object, retained 18–24 months unless Field Audit Trail is licensed. It is the limit most data-migration plans discover late.
How often can a Full Copy sandbox be refreshed?
Full Copy: every 29 days. Partial Copy: every 5 days. Developer and Developer Pro: once a day.
Which sandbox type copies a sample of production data chosen by a sandbox template?
A Partial Copy sandbox takes metadata plus a sample of records defined by a sandbox template. Developer and Developer Pro copy metadata only; a scratch org is not a sandbox.
How many profiles can one user have?
Exactly one profile per user. Anything more is added with permission sets and permission set groups, which is why least-privilege designs keep the profile minimal.
What does a permission set group let an admin do?
Bundle several permission sets and assign them as one
Give a user a second profile
Override organisation-wide defaults for a group of users
Share records with a public group
A permission set group bundles permission sets for a job role. A muting permission set inside the group can switch off individual permissions the bundle would otherwise grant.
With "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" on, what does the role hierarchy give a manager?
Access to records owned by users below them in the hierarchy
Access to records owned by users above them
Edit access to every record of every object
The ability to change subordinates’ profiles
Access rolls UP the hierarchy: a manager sees what their subordinates own. It never gives a subordinate access to the manager’s records.
A sharing rule can be based on which of these?
Who owns the record, or field values on the record
The page layout assigned to the record
Owner-based sharing rules share records owned by a group or role; criteria-based sharing rules share records whose field values match. Both only open access beyond the default.
Field-level security lives on profiles and permission sets. Sharing decides WHICH records; field-level security decides which FIELDS on them.
An admin removes a field from every page layout. What changes for API access to that field?
Nothing — layouts are not security; field-level security still decides
The field becomes read-only through the API
The field is hidden from the API and reports
The field is encrypted at rest
A page layout only arranges the record page. A user whose field-level security allows the field can still read it through the API, reports and list views.
What do the organisation’s Trusted IP Ranges (Network Access) do?
Block every login from outside the ranges
Let users log in from those addresses without being asked to verify their identity
Restrict API calls to those addresses only
Allow guest users to see internal records
Trusted IP ranges skip the identity-verification challenge; they do not block anything. To refuse logins from elsewhere, set Login IP Ranges on the profile.
Between which orgs can change sets be deployed?
Orgs affiliated with the same production org, connected by a deployment connection
Change sets move metadata between a production org and its sandboxes (or between those sandboxes), and only along an authorised deployment connection.
A validation rule blocks the save when its formula returns what?
The formula describes the INVALID state: TRUE means "this record is wrong", and the save is refused with the rule’s message.
What do record types primarily control?
Which records a user can see
Which picklist values and page layout a user gets for a record
Record types offer different business processes, picklist values and page layouts. They are not a security control; sharing still decides visibility.
Named users manage users in specified roles and profiles without full admin rights
Any user can create custom objects
A partner org administers your org
Admins log in without multi-factor authentication
A delegated administration group lets, say, a regional manager reset passwords and assign permission sets for their own users without System Administrator.
Which permission lets a user read every record in the org regardless of sharing?
View All Data bypasses sharing for reading every object. It is the permission an access review should look for first.
How are records shared with the unauthenticated guest user of a site?
By putting the guest user in the role hierarchy
By making the guest user a record owner
Through manual sharing from the record
Guest users get record access only through guest user sharing rules (criteria-based). They cannot be in the role hierarchy or own records, which keeps public exposure explicit.
Besides a user, what can own a record such as a lead or case?
A queue can own records of the objects it supports; its members pick work from it. Roles, profiles and permission sets never own records.
What can a public group contain?
Users, roles, roles and subordinates, and other groups
Public groups gather users, roles (with or without subordinates) and other groups, so one sharing rule can target all of them.
Where would an admin see who changed a validation rule last week?
Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes and who made them, for the last 180 days. Field history tracks data changes, not setup.
How must an object’s default external access compare with its default internal access?
External organisation-wide defaults can never be more open than the internal ones, so external users never see more than employees by default.
In a master-detail relationship, what decides who can see a detail record?
The master record — sharing is "Controlled by Parent"
A separate sharing rule on the detail object
Detail records have no owner of their own; access follows the master. That is the practical difference from a lookup when designing security.
What does a muting permission set do inside a permission set group?
Grants every permission in the group twice
Turns off selected permissions that the group's other permission sets grant
Muting lets one group serve a job role that needs most, but not all, of a bundle's permissions, without building a second bundle.
By default, who can manually share a record?
Its owner, users above the owner in the role hierarchy, and administrators
Any user who can see it
Only the user who created it
Manual sharing comes from full access to the record: the owner, those above them in the hierarchy and anyone with Modify All.
A user owns a contact on an account they cannot otherwise see. What access do they get to that account?
Full edit access to the account
Read-only access to the parent account
Implicit (parent) sharing gives read access to the account so the child record makes sense; it never grants edit.
What happens to a signed-in user when the login hours on their profile end?
Nothing until they close the browser
Their session is extended by an hour
Their next action logs them out
Login hours are enforced on the next request after the window closes, so a user cannot keep working past them.
Which of these is a valid multi-factor authentication method for Salesforce logins?
A push from the Salesforce Authenticator app
Salesforce MFA accepts authenticator apps, security keys and built-in authenticators; email and SMS codes do not satisfy the MFA requirement.
What is a connected app for?
Letting an external application integrate with Salesforce using OAuth
Linking a user to a second profile
Publishing a site to the internet
A connected app defines how an outside application authenticates, which OAuth scopes it gets and which policies apply.
Where does Shield Platform Encryption encrypt data?
Only in transit between browser and server
Data is already encrypted in transit; Shield Platform Encryption adds encryption at rest for chosen fields, files and more.
A list of upcoming calendar events
Detailed event log files, such as logins, report exports and API calls
Event log files show who did what — exports, API usage, page views — which is what an investigation needs.
What does Security Health Check compare an org's settings against?
A security baseline — Salesforce's standard or a custom one
Health Check scores password, session and network settings against a baseline and lists the risks to fix.
What happens to the records a user owns when the user is deactivated?
They keep the records; ownership does not change automatically
The records move to the admin
Deactivation stops the login only. Reassigning ownership is a separate, deliberate step.
Can a user record be deleted in Salesforce?
Yes, but only in a sandbox
No — users are deactivated or frozen, never deleted
User records stay so that ownership, history and audit trails keep pointing at somebody.
What does freezing a user do?
Stops them logging in straight away, without deactivating them
Freeze is the immediate stop while a deactivation (which can be blocked by dependencies) is sorted out.
How much data storage does a Developer sandbox have?
Developer: 200 MB. Developer Pro: 1 GB. Partial Copy: 5 GB. Full Copy: the same as production.
What is the maximum lifespan of a scratch org?
Scratch orgs default to 7 days and can be created for up to 30; they are disposable by design.
Which tool deploys and retrieves metadata from the command line?
The Salesforce CLI (sf) drives source-driven development: deploy, retrieve, run tests and create scratch orgs.
What does Quick Deploy rely on?
A deployment with no Apex at all
A successful validation, with tests passed, in the last 10 days
A validated deployment can be quick-deployed within 10 days without running the tests again.
When a deployment to production includes Apex and no test level is given, which tests run?
Only the tests in the deployment
Production defaults to RunLocalTests: every test in the org except those from managed packages.
What do Dynamic Forms let an admin do?
Place fields and sections on the Lightning page and show them by visibility rules
Let users design their own layouts
Fields become components on the Lightning page, so a section can appear only when it is relevant.
What limits the values in one picklist based on the value of another field?
A dependent picklist with a controlling field
The controlling field decides which values the dependent picklist offers.
What is a global value set?
A set of default field values for every object
One list of picklist values shared by several fields
Several picklists can use one value list, so the values stay identical everywhere they appear.
What does a restricted picklist enforce?
Only values from its defined list can be saved, including through the API
It can hold one value only
Without the restriction, an API load can write any text into a picklist, which reports then show as a value nobody defined.
When is a formula field's value calculated?
When it is read — it is not stored
Once, when the record is created
Only when the record is edited
Formulas are computed on read, so they always reflect the current data and cost no storage.
How is a many-to-many relationship modelled between two objects?
A junction object with two master-detail relationships
Each junction record links one record from each side, like a line connecting a contact to a campaign.
How many master-detail relationships can a custom object have?
Two — enough for a junction object. Lookup relationships are far more generous.
By default, what happens to an optional lookup when the parent record is deleted?
The lookup field on the child is cleared
The child moves to the Recycle Bin
"Clear the value of this field" is the default for an optional lookup; master-detail cascades the delete instead.
Viewing and editing objects, fields and relationships on a diagram
It shows the data model visually and can create objects and fields from the canvas.
Which can be deployed with its records from one org to another, like configuration?
Custom metadata records are metadata, so they move in change sets and packages; custom setting data does not.
A hierarchy custom setting lets a value vary by what?
The most specific level wins: a user value beats a profile value, which beats the org default.
What does a report type define?
Which objects, relationships and fields a report can use
A report type sets the primary object, its related objects and the fields available — and whether related records must exist.
On a standard dashboard, what does the running user decide?
Whose data access the dashboard shows
Everyone viewing a standard dashboard sees the data as the running user would. A dynamic dashboard shows it as the viewer.
Whose data does a dynamic dashboard show?
The last person who refreshed it
Each viewer sees only what their own access allows, which suits one dashboard for many managers.
What does a reporting snapshot do?
Takes a picture of a dashboard
Saves a report's results into a custom object on a schedule
Freezes a report so nobody can edit it
Snapshots build history — pipeline at the start of each week, say — that live reports cannot show.
What can a joined report do?
Show several blocks, each from its own report type, in one report
Each block has its own report type and filters; common fields let them be grouped together.
What do duplicate rules use to identify possible duplicates?
A matching rule says what counts as the same record; the duplicate rule decides whether to alert or block.
Showing prompts and walkthroughs to users inside the app
Prompts and walkthroughs explain a change where people work, instead of in an email they will not read.
When does a login flow run?
Only when a password is reset
After the user authenticates, before they reach the app
A login flow can ask for extra information, show terms, or add a verification step after authentication.
Users sign in to Salesforce with their company identity provider over SAML. What role does Salesforce play?
The identity provider authenticates the user and asserts who they are; Salesforce, as service provider, trusts that assertion.
Which is true of My Domain today?
Every org has one, giving it its own login URL
It is optional and rarely used
It is only for Experience Cloud
My Domain is now required for every org; it is what SSO, Lightning components and custom login policies are built on.
